title: Optimise NPS for Higher Returns & a Bigger Retirement Corpus

faq.q: What is the minimum contribution to NPS Tier I?
faq.a: The minimum contribution required for an NPS Tier I account is ₹500 per transaction, with a minimum aggregate contribution of ₹1,000 in a financial year.

faq.q: Can I change my NPS asset allocation?
faq.a: Yes, you can change your asset allocation strategy (from Active to Auto or vice-versa) and modify your allocation percentages within Active Choice once a financial year. You can also change your Pension Fund Manager once a year.

faq.q: How many Pension Fund Managers can I choose?
faq.a: You can choose one Pension Fund Manager (PFM) for your NPS account. However, you have the flexibility to switch your PFM once a year if you wish to.

faq.q: What happens to my NPS corpus upon retirement?
faq.a: Upon reaching age 60, you can withdraw up to 60% of your NPS corpus as a tax-free lump sum. The remaining minimum 40% must be used to purchase an annuity plan from an IRDAI-regulated life insurance company, which provides a regular pension.

faq.q: Is NPS suitable for short-term goals?
faq.a: No, NPS is designed as a long-term retirement savings instrument with a lock-in period until age 60 for Tier I accounts. It is not suitable for short-term financial goals due to its illiquid nature and withdrawal restrictions.
Yes, Non-Resident Indians (NRIs) can open an NPS account. They can contribute to NPS using their NRE/NRO accounts. The rules for withdrawal and taxation are generally similar to resident Indians.

faq.q: What is the difference between NPS and EPF?
faq.a: EPF (Employees' Provident Fund) is mandatory for most salaried employees, with fixed contributions and returns. NPS is a voluntary, market-linked pension scheme with flexible contributions and asset allocation choices, offering different tax benefits and withdrawal rules.

fact_check.summary: The article provides a generally reliable overview of NPS, its structure, tax benefits, asset allocation, and withdrawal rules. Most factual claims are accurate and align with authoritative sources.

corrections.note: Corrected the frequency of changing NPS asset allocation and updated the NPS withdrawal rules for both government and non-government subscribers based on recent amendments.

edits.why: NPS subscribers can change their asset allocation up to four times in a financial year, not once. The ability to change PFM once a year is correct.

The withdrawal rules for NPS have been updated. For non-government subscribers, if the corpus is above ₹12 lakh, at least 20% must be used for an annuity, and up to 80% can be withdrawn as a lump sum. If the corpus is up to ₹8 lakh, the entire amount can be withdrawn. The 60% tax-free lump sum and 40% annuity rule still applies to government employees.
